newsitem.title: INDIA: BUDGET HIGHLIGHTS - India infrastructure proposals.
newsitem.headline: BUDGET HIGHLIGHTS - India infrastructure proposals.

text.p: Following are the highlights of India's infrastructure proposals announced by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in the annual budget for 1997/98 (April-March) on Friday.
-- Oil Exploration and Industrial Parks included in the Infrastructure sector.
-- Assignability of telecom licence issue resolved. Tripartite agreements proposed to be entered into among DoT, licencee and lenders.
-- Budgetary support to National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) enhanced to Rs.500 crore.
-- Proposal for service tax on transportation of goods by road for development of National Highways.
-- Supplies of goods to oil, gas and power projects made under international competitive bidding procedure to be given the benefits of deemed exports.
-- Rs.2500 crore Rural Infrastructure Development Fund - III to be launched during the financial year.
-- Tax holiday for infrastructure projects to continue.
-- The share of the Central Government from the proceeds of the Voluntary Disclosure of black money Scheme during the year to be utilised to finance infrastructure needs.

-- Deduction of 50% of profit of new hotels in hilly areas, rural areas, places of pilgrimage or a specified place of tourist importance. These hotels also to be exempted from levy of expenditure tax. In case of hotels located in other places, excluding the four metropolitan cities, deduction to be 30% of the profits.
-- Reduction of duty on non-coking coal from 20% to 10% to benefit power sector.
-- To help control vehicular pollution, sharp reduction of custom duty on catalytic converters from 25% to a modest 5%. Custom duty reduced on import of CNG kits and their parts from 10% to 5%.
